One-Pot Vegan Enchilada Skillet

by Sarah Rotavera on October 9, 2026
Jump to Recipe Leave a Review Pin Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:04
Instaread

A deconstructed version of plant-based enchiladas that comes together in one skillet. Requiring just 30-minutes to make, it’s the perfect quick easy weeknight meal! (high-protein + gluten-free)

MY LATEST VIDEOS

Video Paused

Enchiladas are one of those meals that I always crave but rarely have the energy to make. Especially now that I’ve been trying to avoid gluten, finding tortillas that are easy to roll without breaking can be a challenge.

Well, this enchilada skillet has been the answer to all of my prayers. It’s ridiculously easy to make and you just cut up the tortillas so it doesn’t really matter if they’re fragile or not. Not to mention, it comes together in just one-pot so clean up is a breeze. We’re winning on all fronts with this one!

One-Pot Enchilada Skillet Ingredients

  • Extra Virgin Olive Oil– or any neutral flavored oil you prefer.
  • Onion and Garlic– white, yellow or red onion all work here.
  • Bell Pepper– I prefer red for its mild sweetness but any color works.
  • Zucchini- a great way to sneak in some green but optional, if desired.
  • Spices– cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika are my go-to for Mexican-inspired recipes.
  • Plant-based Ground “Beef”– I’m obsessed with Abbot’s products because they’re packed with protein, made with simple ingredients and the flavor is incredible. If you’re not into isolated protein sources, you could easy substitute 8-ounces of finely chopped cremini mushrooms or a batch of my Easy Tofu Ground “Beef”crumbles.
  • Tortillas– I prefer to use pure corn tortillas as they’re naturally gluten-free and the texture holds up well when soaked in enchilada sauce.
  • Black Beans– for extra protein and fiber. I like Jovial’s beans because they’re in glass jars and avoid microplastics.
  • Enchilada Sauce– Siete’s red enchilada sauce is elite.

How to Make One-Pot Skillet Enchiladas

**For full recipe instructions, scroll down to recipe card below**

Save this Recipe

We'll email this post to you, so you can come back to it later!

  1. Warm oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and sauté until translucent.
  2. Next, add the plant-based crumbles (or mushrooms). Cook, while stirring intermittently, for 5 minutes.
  3. Add the bell pepper, zucchini and garlic then sprinkle with spices.
  4. Cover and cook, for 5-7 minutes, until zucchini is softened.
  5. Top with sliced tortillas, black beans and enchilada sauce. Stir carefully until the tortillas are coated in the sauce.
  6. Cover and cook for 10 minutes more.
  7. Sprinkle with cheese and cover again, until cheese has melted.
  8. Serve with desired toppings and enjoy!

One-Pot Vegan Enchilada Skillet

Sarah Rotavera
4 servings
A deconstructed version of plant-based enchiladas that comes together in just 30-minutes! (gluten-free)
Print Recipe Pin Recipe Leave a Review
Prep Time: 10 minutes mins
Cook Time: 20 minutes mins
Total Time: 30 minutes mins

Ingredients
 

  • 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
  • 1 small red onion, finely chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 10-ounce package plant-based ground "beef", can sub cremini mushrooms
  • 1 small to medium zucchini , finely chopped
  • 1 red bell pepper, cored and finely chopped
  • 1 teaspoon cumin
  • 1 teaspoon chili powder
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 8 corn tortillas, cut into triangles
  • 15 ounces black beans, drained and rinsed
  • 15 ounces enchilada sauce
  • ½ cup shredded cheese, dairy-free
  • serving suggestions: avocado, cilantro, pickled onions, or dairy-free yogurt

Instructions
 

  • In a large skillet, warm the oil over medium-low heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
  • To the skillet, add the plant-based crumbles. Stir and continue to cook for 5 minutes, more.
  • Add the chopped zucchini, bell pepper, and garlic. Sprinkle with 1 teaspoon ground cumin, chili powder and smoked paprika. Stir to combine. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until zucchini is softened.
  • Remove the lid and spread the tortilla triangles over top. Place the drained black beans on top then cover with enchilada sauce. Stir together until tortillas are evenly coated in sauce. Cover with the lid and cook for 10 minutes more.
  • Lastly, sprinkle with shredded cheese and cover again with the lid. Cook for a few minutes, until the cheese has melted.
  • Serve warm with desired toppings, and enjoy!
